unit.label: Tea & conversation
unit.title: A little conversation over tea.
unit.description: 8 new words and expressions. Offer a drink, share a preference, and say thanks.

goal.pinyin: nǐ yào bu yào hē chá?

unit.bookReference: Book 1 · Lesson 1: drinks, preferences & polite conversation

lessons.title: A cup of conversation
lessons.subtitle: Drink tea and say how it tastes

steps.explanation: 茶 is chá, tea, with a rising second tone.

lessons.title: Please have some tea
lessons.subtitle: Make a polite offer with 請

steps.prompt: You are offering tea to a guest. Which expression fits?
steps.explanation: 請 comes before 喝茶 to make a polite invitation.
請 is qǐng, with the third tone. It introduces a polite request or invitation.

steps.prompt: Which component do 請 and 說 share?
steps.explanation: 言 is the speech component on the left of both 請 and 說.

steps.prompt: Which sentence describes enjoying reading, rather than wanting to read now?
steps.explanation: 喜歡 describes liking the activity. 想 expresses wanting; 會 expresses a learned ability.
歡 is huān, the second character of 喜歡.

lessons.title: Would you like coffee?
lessons.subtitle: A new drink and another way to ask

steps.prompt: Which is a complete A-not-A question?
steps.explanation: 要不要 already forms the question. Do not add 嗎.

steps.prompt: 你要不要喝茶？ You want some. Choose the short answer.
steps.explanation: Repeat 要 because the question asks whether you want tea.

lessons.title: And you?
lessons.subtitle: Keep the conversation going with 呢

steps.prompt: Someone says they like reading and adds 你呢？ What are they asking?
steps.explanation: 呢 carries the same topic over to you. The preceding conversation supplies the missing question.
呢 is neutral-tone ne here. Compare neutral-tone ma in 嗎.

lessons.title: Thank you
lessons.subtitle: Respond politely and bring it together

steps.prompt: You are handed a drink. Choose a simple way to thank the person.
steps.explanation: 謝謝你 directly thanks the person. 你呢 returns a topic as a question.

steps.prompt: 你喜歡咖啡嗎？ You do not like coffee. Choose the short answer.
steps.explanation: Repeat the questioned verb with 不: 不喜歡. This question is about a preference.
謝 is xiè, with a falling fourth tone.

steps.prompt: 她是不是學生？ She is not a student. Choose the short answer.
steps.explanation: 是不是 asks about identity, so answer with 是 or 不是.

喝.note: 喝 is the action drink. The drink follows it directly: 喝茶.
喝.memory: Keep the mouth narrow and leave room for the right side.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 relates to using the mouth. Here the action is drinking.

parts.label: 曷
parts.name: historical sound part
parts.description: 曷 is the historical phonetic component. Learn hē with the whole character; modern sounds are not identical.

茶.note: 茶 names tea. In this Taiwan stroke form, the grass top takes four strokes.
茶.memory: Start with the grass, then the spreading middle and lower strokes.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass top
parts.description: This plant-related component helps connect the character with tea leaves.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower shape
parts.description: Learn the remaining strokes as one visual group. Their shapes are not a literal formula for tea.

請.note: Put 請 before an action to make a polite invitation or request.
請.memory: Recognize the speech component on the left, with 青 on the right.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech
parts.description: 言 is the speech component, a useful clue for this polite expression.

parts.label: 青
parts.name: qīng sound part
parts.description: 青 (qīng) suggests the qing syllable. 請 has the third tone.

喜.note: Use 喜 with 歡 as the everyday word 喜歡, to like.
喜.memory: Build the upper group, then finish with the lower mouth.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The first nine strokes form the upper group. Use its stacked shapes as a memory aid.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth shape
parts.description: The last three strokes form a separate 口 at the bottom.

歡.note: 歡 completes 喜歡. Learn the two characters as one word for like.
歡.memory: Give the dense left side most of the space and keep 欠 slim.

parts.label: 雚
parts.name: guàn sound part
parts.description: 雚 is a historical phonetic component. The modern sound differs, so learn huān with the whole word.

parts.label: 欠
parts.name: qiàn component
parts.description: 欠 is the four-stroke component on the right. Recognizing it helps organize this dense character.

咖.note: 咖啡 is a borrowed word for coffee. Here 咖 is pronounced kā.
咖.memory: Spot the mouth next to 加.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 appears in many characters used for sounds and spoken words.

parts.label: 加
parts.name: jiā sound-related part
parts.description: 加 is the phonetic component historically. In the borrowed word 咖啡, learn the pronunciation kā.

啡.note: 啡 completes 咖啡. The two characters form one word.
啡.memory: A small mouth sits beside the balanced rows of 非.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: This is the same left component as in 咖 and 喝.

parts.label: 非
parts.name: fēi sound part
parts.description: 非 (fēi) points directly to the pronunciation of 啡.

呢.note: Here 呢 asks the same question about another person: 你呢？ means And you?
呢.memory: A mouth on the left and 尼 on the right.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 is common in spoken sentence particles, including 嗎 and 呢.

parts.label: 尼
parts.name: ní sound part
parts.description: 尼 is the historical phonetic component. In this particle, use neutral-tone ne.

謝.note: The everyday expression is 謝謝. The second syllable is often light: xièxie.
謝.memory: Keep 言 narrow; let 射 fill the right side.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech
parts.description: The same speech component appears in 請 and 說. Thanking is expressed in words.

parts.label: 射
parts.name: shè sound part
parts.description: 射 is a historical sound component. Its modern pronunciation differs from xiè.

u5-drink.title: Talk about a drink
u5-drink.explanation: 喝 works like 看 and 聽: put the thing after the action. 茶 names tea generally; no measure word is needed when saying what you drink.
u5-drink.remember: 不 goes before 喝. Do not add 是 before an action.

u5-taste.title: Say a drink tastes good
u5-taste.explanation: 好喝 means pleasant to drink. Treat it as a describing word, like 大 and 小. 很 connects the subject and the description in a neutral statement; stronger stress can make it mean very.
u5-taste.remember: Use 好喝 for drinks. You already know 好, but learn 好喝 as a whole expression. No 是 is needed.

u5-please.title: Offer something politely
u5-please.explanation: Place 請 before an action when inviting someone to do it politely. With a drink, this is a way to offer it to your guest. The person you address is often left unstated.
u5-please.remember: 請 introduces the invitation; it is not a question particle and does not go at the end.

u5-likes.title: Say what you like
u5-likes.explanation: 喜歡 means like. It can be followed by a thing or by an action phrase. Put 不 before the entire word to say dislike or do not like.
u5-likes.remember: 喜歡 is a preference; 想 is a wish to do something. 喜歡喝茶 says you enjoy drinking tea, not that you want tea right now.

u5-coffee.title: Tea and coffee
u5-coffee.explanation: 咖啡 is coffee, a two-character borrowed word. Both syllables have the first tone. Use the same action and preference patterns with this new drink.
u5-coffee.remember: 咖 and 啡 are character parts of one vocabulary word; do not translate them separately.

u5-a-not-a.title: Ask with an action and its negative
u5-a-not-a.explanation: You can form a yes/no question by giving the positive and negative versions of the first verb. Use 要不要 to ask about wanting, 喝不喝 about drinking, and 是不是 about identity. The object stays at the end.

examples.pinyin: nǐ yào bu yào hē chá?

u5-a-not-a.remember: Choose this structure OR a statement followed by 嗎. Do not combine them. 不 is often light in A-not-A questions; pinyin here shows neutral bu.

u5-answers.title: Give a short answer
u5-answers.pattern: repeat the questioned verb / 不 + verb
u5-answers.explanation: Answer a simple yes/no question by repeating the verb that was questioned. For 要不要, use 要 or 不要. For a question about liking, use 喜歡 or 不喜歡. English yes does not always become 是.

examples.pinyin: nǐ yào bu yào hē chá? yào
nǐ xǐhuān kāfēi ma? bù xǐhuān

u5-answers.remember: Use 是 or 不是 for an identity question with 是. The negative of 有 remains 沒有, as you learned earlier.

u5-follow-up.title: Ask “and you?”
u5-follow-up.explanation: After someone states a preference or answers a question, use another person followed by 呢 to return the same topic to them. The earlier sentence supplies what you are asking about.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xǐhuān kàn shū. nǐ ne?

examples.meaning: I drink tea. What about him?

u5-follow-up.remember: 呢 is light and neutral here. It needs context; it is not an interchangeable replacement for 嗎.

u5-thanks.title: Say thank you
u5-thanks.explanation: 謝謝 is the common expression for thanking someone. You can add the person directly, as in 謝謝你. The second syllable is often light in everyday speech.
u5-thanks.remember: Write 謝 twice, but count 謝謝 as one expression. No 的 or 是 is needed.

u5-taste.note: Use 很 before the description; no 是.

u5-like-read.note: 喜歡 can take an action phrase.

u5-dislike-tea.note: 不 goes before the whole word 喜歡.

u5-coffee.note: 咖啡 stays together as one word.

u5-want-tea.pinyin: nǐ yào bu yào hē chá?
u5-want-tea.note: Both copies of 要 belong in the sentence. Do not add 嗎.

u5-want-coffee.pinyin: nǐ yào bu yào hē kāfēi?
u5-want-coffee.note: Repeat the first verb, 要. Keep 喝咖啡 at the end.

u5-and-you.note: Use after a statement or answer to return the same topic.

u5-and-her.note: The preceding conversation tells us what is being asked.

u5-thanks.note: The person being thanked follows 謝謝.

u5-thanks-all.note: 你們 addresses more than one person.
